description: This file defines the base class ADODB_DataDict for generating SQL data definition language (DDL) statements specific to various databases, as part of the ADOdb database abstraction layer. It includes functions for creating, altering, dropping tables and columns, managing indexes, and parsing SQL-like argument strings. It also contains a test function and some utility functions.

classes.name: ADODB_DataDict
classes.description: A base class for generating database-specific DDL SQL statements in the ADOdb PHP library, providing methods to create, modify, and drop tables, columns, indexes, and other schema objects.

methods.name: getCommentSQL
methods.description: Returns the SQL statement to get comment for a specific column (not implemented, returns false).

methods.name: setCommentSQL
methods.description: Returns the SQL statement to set comment for a specific column (not implemented, returns false).

methods.name: metaTables
methods.description: Returns the list of tables in the current database connection.

methods.name: metaColumns
methods.description: Returns metadata for columns of a specified table.

methods.name: metaPrimaryKeys
methods.description: Returns primary key columns for a specified table.

methods.name: metaIndexes
methods.description: Returns index information for a specified table.

methods.name: metaType
methods.description: Returns the mapped meta type for a given database type string.

methods.name: nameQuote
methods.description: Quotes a given identifier name for use in SQL statements, considering whether to allow brackets.

methods.name: tableName
methods.description: Constructs a fully qualified table name, including schema if set.

methods.name: executeSQLArray
methods.description: Executes an array of SQL statements, optionally continuing on errors.

methods.name: actualType
methods.description: Returns the actual meta type code for a given type string, optionally overridden by custom types.

methods.name: createDatabase
methods.description: Generates SQL to create a new database.

methods.name: createIndexSQL
methods.description: Generates SQL to create an index on a table.

methods.name: dropIndexSQL
methods.description: Generates SQL to drop an index.

methods.name: setSchema
methods.description: Sets the schema name for qualified naming.

methods.name: addColumnSQL
methods.description: Generates SQL to add columns to an existing table.

methods.name: alterColumnSQL
methods.description: Generates SQL to alter existing columns in a table.

methods.name: renameColumnSQL
methods.description: Generates SQL to rename a column in a table.

methods.name: dropColumnSQL
methods.description: Generates SQL to drop columns from a table.

methods.name: dropTableSQL
methods.description: Generates SQL to drop a table.

methods.name: renameTableSQL
methods.description: Generates SQL to rename a table.

methods.name: createTableSQL
methods.description: Generates SQL to create a new table with specified fields and options.

methods.name: _genFields
methods.description: Parses field definitions and generates SQL column definitions, primary keys, and index info.

methods.name: _getSize
methods.description: Constructs the size part of a data type declaration.

methods.name: _createSuffix
methods.description: Constructs constraints and options for a column.

methods.name: _indexSQL
methods.description: Constructs index creation or drop SQL statements.

methods.name: _dropAutoIncrement
methods.description: Placeholder for dropping auto-increment sequences; default returns false.

methods.name: _tableSQL
methods.description: Constructs the SQL to create a table with columns and constraints.

methods.name: _triggers
methods.description: Placeholder for generating triggers for auto-increment emulation; default returns empty array.

methods.name: _options
methods.description: Sanitizes and normalizes table options array.

methods.name: _getSizePrec
methods.description: Parses size and precision from a string.

methods.name: changeTableSQL
methods.description: Generates SQL commands to modify an existing table schema, adding, altering, or dropping fields.
